faqs.question: What is the admission procedure for undergraduate B.Tech programs?
patterns: How do I apply for BTech admission?
What is the admission process for engineering?
B.Tech admission steps and requirements
How to take admission in undergraduate courses?
Engineering admission procedure
faqs.answer: Undergraduate B.Tech admissions are based on national or state entrance test scores (such as JEE Main or State CET) followed by centralized counseling. Candidates must submit an online application on the college admissions portal, upload required academic documents, and participate in document verification during the designated counseling rounds.

faqs.question: What are the minimum eligibility criteria for B.Tech and MCA courses?
patterns: What is the eligibility for B.Tech and MCA?
Minimum marks required for admission
BTech and MCA cutoff percentage criteria
Am I eligible for admission with 60 percent?
Criteria for engineering and MCA admissions
faqs.answer: For B.Tech: Candidates must have passed 10+2 with Physics, Mathematics, and Chemistry/Computer Science with at least 60% aggregate marks (55% for reserved categories). For MCA: Candidates must hold a recognized Bachelor's degree (BCA/B.Sc/B.Com/B.A.) with Mathematics at 10+2 or graduation level and a minimum of 50% aggregate.

faqs.question: Can I get direct admission through management quota or lateral entry?
patterns: Is there management quota admission?

faqs.answer: Yes. Diploma holders in Engineering with at least 50% marks can apply for Direct Second Year (Lateral Entry) into B.Tech programs. A limited percentage of seats is also available under the institutional/management quota as per state regulatory guidelines.

faqs.answer: The institute offers B.Tech programs in Computer Science & Engineering (CSE), Artificial Intelligence & Data Science (AI-DS), Electronics & Telecommunication (ENTC), Mechanical Engineering, and Information Technology. Postgraduate offerings include M.Tech, MBA, and MCA.

faqs.question: What is the mandatory attendance requirement to appear for semester exams?
patterns: What is the minimum attendance required?
Is 75 percent attendance mandatory?

Attendance policy for semester examinations
What happens if my attendance is below 75 percent?
faqs.answer: Students must maintain a minimum of 75% attendance in theory lectures and practical labs separately for each subject. Students falling between 65% and 74% due to verified medical conditions must submit certified medical documents. Those below 65% may be detained from appearing in end-semester examinations.

faqs.question: How is the academic grading system and CGPA calculated?
patterns: How is CGPA calculated from SGPA?
What is the grading scale used in college?
How to convert CGPA to percentage?
Credit system and GPA calculation formula
faqs.answer: The institute follows a 10-point relative grading scale: O (Outstanding = 10), A+ (Excellent = 9), A (Very Good = 8), B+ (Good = 7), B (Above Average = 6), C (Average = 5), P (Pass = 4), and F (Fail = 0). SGPA is computed as sum(Credits * Grade Points) / Total Credits for that semester. Percentage approximation is typically (CGPA * 9.5) or as per university ordinance.

faqs.answer: Annual tuition fees for B.Tech programs are approximately ₹1,20,000 per academic year for general category students (divided across two semester installments). Laboratory, library, development, and student activity fees total approximately ₹25,000 per year. (Note: These figures are sample demo data).

faqs.answer: Students can apply for: 1) State & National Scholarship Portal (NSP) schemes for SC/ST/OBC/EWS candidates, 2) Institute Merit Scholarships offering up to 50% tuition waiver for semester rank-holders with CGPA > 9.0, and 3) Special corporate sponsored scholarships for girl students in STEM and sports achievers.

faqs.question: What modes of payment are accepted for tuition fees, and are installments allowed?
patterns: How can I pay my college fees online?
Can I pay semester fees in installments?

Fee payment portal and bank transfer options
faqs.answer: Fees can be paid online via the College ERP Student Portal using Net Banking, UPI, Debit/Credit cards, or offline via Bank Demand Draft (DD) in favor of the college. Split installment requests (up to two parts per semester) can be submitted to the accounts section with prior approval from the Dean of Student Affairs.

faqs.question: What is the fee refund policy if an admission is cancelled?
patterns: What is the refund policy on admission cancellation?
Can I get my fee back if I withdraw my seat?
Refund rules and deduction amount
How long does fee refund take after cancellation?
faqs.answer: Fee refunds strictly follow UGC guidelines: 100% refund (with deduction of max ₹1,000 processing fee) if cancelled 15 days or more before the formally announced last date of admission; 90% if less than 15 days before; 80% within 15 days after; 50% between 16 and 30 days; and no refund after 30 days from the deadline.

faqs.question: How are internal assessments and end-semester exams evaluated?
patterns: What is the exam pattern and marking scheme?
How are internal marks and external marks divided?
Weightage of mid-term tests and end semester
Evaluation criteria for theory and practical subjects
faqs.answer: Evaluation consists of continuous internal assessment (40% weightage) and end-semester university examinations (60% weightage). Internals include two midterm tests, continuous lab assessment, mini-projects/assignments, and class participation. A minimum of 40% in end-sem and 40% aggregate is required to pass a course.

faqs.question: What is the policy for ATKT, backlogs, and re-examinations?
patterns: What are the rules for clearing backlogs?
How many backlogs are allowed for ATKT promotion?
When are supplementary or backlog exams held?
Re-exam policy for failed subjects
Can I get promoted to next year with backlogs?
faqs.answer: Students can carry a maximum of 4 active backlogs (ATKT - Allowed to Keep Term) into the subsequent academic year. Supplementary re-examinations are conducted within 45 days of the semester result declaration. Final year students must clear all backlogs before graduation to receive the degree.

faqs.question: How can I apply for photocopy or revaluation of exam answer sheets?
patterns: How to apply for paper rechecking or revaluation?
Re-evaluation procedure and fee per subject
Can I see my evaluated exam answer sheet?
Paper verification and recount process
faqs.answer: Students dissatisfied with exam marks can apply for revaluation or obtain an evaluated digital copy via the Exam Cell portal within 10 days of result announcement. A non-refundable processing fee of ₹300 per subject applies. If marks change by more than 10%, the revised grade is updated in the marksheet.

faqs.question: Is an internship mandatory for engineering students, and for what duration?
patterns: Are internships mandatory in engineering?
How long should the summer internship be?

Do 3rd year students have to do an internship?
Industrial training requirements
faqs.answer: Yes. As per AICTE guidelines, students must complete at least 6 to 8 weeks of industrial training or internship during the summer breaks after the 4th or 6th semester. Final-year students in the 8th semester may also opt for a full-semester 6-month industry internship with company sponsorship and department approval.

faqs.question: How does the Training & Placement Cell help students find internships?

faqs.answer: The T&P Cell organizes an annual Internship Fair, coordinates with industry partners, and regularly posts verified internship openings on the student placement portal. The cell also provides bonafide Recommendation Letters (NOC) required by external organizations.

faqs.question: How do I get a No Objection Certificate (NOC) for an off-campus internship?

faqs.answer: To obtain an NOC: 1) Submit the company's official internship offer letter along with job role and duration to your Department Training Coordinator, 2) Ensure attendance and academic criteria are met, and 3) Once approved by the Head of Department (HOD), the T&P Cell issues the signed institutional NOC.

faqs.question: What is the minimum CGPA and academic criteria to be eligible for placements?
patterns: What is the minimum CGPA required for campus placement?
Placement eligibility criteria for students
Can a student with 6.5 CGPA sit for placements?
Minimum pointer required for campus drives
Eligibility percentage in 10th 12th for placements
faqs.answer: While the college permits students with a CGPA >= 6.0 and no active backlogs to register for T&P drives, individual companies set their own cutoffs: Mass recruiters usually require 60% (or 6.0-6.5 CGPA) throughout 10th, 12th, and B.Tech. Top product companies and tier-1 firms typically mandate a CGPA of 7.5 or 8.0+.

faqs.question: Can students with active or history of backlogs participate in campus drives?
patterns: Can I sit for placements if I have backlogs?
Do companies allow students with active arrears?
Does history of dead backlogs affect placements?
Backlog rules in campus placement drives
faqs.answer: Most companies mandate zero active (standing) backlogs at the time of the drive. Some companies additionally require no past history of backlogs (all subjects cleared in the first attempt). However, select IT service companies and startups permit students with up to 1 cleared backlog to participate.

faqs.question: What is the One Student, One Job policy or Dream Offer policy?
patterns: What is the one student one job rule?
Can I sit for another company after getting placed?
What is a dream company offer policy?
Multiple placement offers policy
Upgrade placement offer rules
faqs.answer: Under the institutional placement policy, once a student secures an offer, they cannot sit for companies in the same salary tier. However, if a student secures a standard offer (< ₹6 LPA), they are eligible to appear for 'Dream Offers' (₹7 to ₹12 LPA) and 'Super Dream Offers' (> ₹12 LPA) up to a maximum of 2 total job offers.

faqs.question: How should I prepare for technical rounds and coding assessments?

faqs.answer: Key focus areas: 1) Master at least one programming language (Java, C++, or Python), 2) Practice Data Structures & Algorithms (Arrays, Linked Lists, Trees, Graphs, Dynamic Programming) on LeetCode/HackerRank, 3) Solidify Core CS Fundamentals (DBMS, OS, Computer Networks, OOP concepts), and 4) Be ready to explain your capstone projects and live architectural choices.

faqs.question: What are the common rounds in a standard campus placement hiring process?
patterns: What are the rounds in campus placement recruitment?
Placement drive hiring stages
Step by step selection process for companies
Aptitude test, technical round, HR round sequence
faqs.answer: A standard campus recruitment drive consists of 4 stages: 1) Online Assessment (Quantitative Aptitude, Logical Reasoning, Verbal Ability, and Coding/Domain MCQs), 2) Technical Interview Round 1 (DSA, problem-solving, live coding), 3) Technical Interview Round 2 / Managerial Round (system design basics, projects, core subjects), and 4) HR Round (cultural fit, behavioral questions, background verification).

faqs.question: How can I build an impactful, ATS-friendly resume for placements?
patterns: How to write a good resume for college placements?
Tips for an ATS friendly resume
Resume format and key sections for freshers
What to include in a student resume?
faqs.answer: To build an effective fresher resume: 1) Keep it to a clean single-page format, 2) Emphasize 2-3 notable projects with GitHub and live demo links using the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result), 3) List technical skills categorized by Languages, Frameworks, Tools, and Databases, 4) Highlight achievements, hackathons, and certifications, and 5) Avoid spelling errors and fancy graphics that disrupt ATS parsing.

faqs.question: How should I tackle HR and behavioral interview questions?
patterns: How to prepare for HR interview questions?
Common questions asked in HR rounds
How to answer 'Tell me about yourself' and 'Where do you see yourself'?
Behavioral interview preparation tips
faqs.answer: Use the STAR technique (Situation, Task, Action, Result) for behavioral answers. Prepare crisp responses for standard prompts like 'Tell me about yourself', 'Why this company?', 'Strengths and weaknesses', and 'Handling conflict in team projects'. Research the company's products, leadership, and culture beforehand, and always prepare 2 thoughtful questions to ask the interviewer.

faqs.question: Does the college conduct mock interviews, aptitude training, and soft skills workshops?
patterns: Does college provide placement training and mock interviews?

faqs.answer: Yes. Starting from the 5th semester, the T&P Cell conducts mandatory Pre-Placement Training (PPT) modules covering quantitative aptitude, logical reasoning, verbal communication, mock group discussions (GD), and one-on-one mock technical and HR interviews with alumni and industry leaders.

faqs.question: What hostel facilities, mess food, and accommodation options are provided?

faqs.answer: Separate on-campus residential hostels are available for boys and girls with 24/7 security, Wi-Fi, laundry facilities, study lounges, and indoor gymnasiums. Rooms are offered on twin and triple-sharing bases. The mess provides hygienic vegetarian and non-vegetarian meal plans inspected by the student mess committee.

faqs.question: What sports facilities, clubs, and cultural activities exist on campus?

faqs.answer: The campus features a multi-sport ground (Cricket, Football, Athletics), basketball and tennis courts, and an indoor sports complex (Badminton, Table Tennis, Chess). Over 20 active student clubs operate on campus, spanning Robotics, Coding, IEEE, Debating, Photography, Drama, and Music, alongside the annual Cultural and Technical Fests.

faqs.answer: The Central Library houses over 50,000 physical volumes, reading halls with 500+ seating capacity, and a Digital Knowledge Center. Students have access to IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, ACM Digital Library, Springer, and DELNET subscriptions. Open on weekdays from 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM and 24/7 during exam weeks.

faqs.question: What medical, healthcare, and emergency facilities are available on campus?

faqs.answer: The college operates a 24/7 Student Health Center staffed by a full-time medical officer and nurses. Basic medical consultations, emergency first-aid, essential medicines, and psychological counseling support are free for enrolled students. A dedicated ambulance is on standby for emergencies with tie-ups at nearby multispecialty hospitals.
